page: Amazon Web Services m5a.24xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by AMD EPYC 7571 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (4.0 GB per core). It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and standard compute, complemented by a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations reveal distinct performance trade-offs inherent to the first-generation AMD EPYC platform. Single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (728.0), stress-ng single-core (591.19), and gzip compression (16.67 GB/sec), register in the lower percentiles due to modest per-core clock rates and IPC. In contrast, parallel capabilities are far more competitive. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 47,126.1 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 7,283.0, with strong results in PassMark CPU encryption (77,560.99) driven by hardware acceleration flags like AES and SHA-NI, as well as Geekbench ray tracing (50,390.0).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m5a.24xlarge offers high core count and aggregate RAM capacity at a lower price point than comparable Intel-based variants, though without support for AVX-512 extensions. The lack of integrated NVMe storage necessitates external EBS attachments for persistent data handling. Workloads well matched to this instance include multi-threaded batch processing, distributed data processing, CI/CD compilation clusters, microservices backends, and multi-tenant web application tiers where aggregate core density and total memory footprint outweigh peak single-threaded execution speeds.
